# Fearless Universal Wallet Project Plan

Last updated: 2026-07-31

This is the cross-repo tracker for the Fearless wallet refactor, new chain support,
indexer work, and git-flow cleanup.

## Status Legend

- Not started: no implementation work has begun.
- In progress: implementation has started but is not release-ready.
- Mitigated: substantial controls are implemented and tested, but a narrower release prerequisite remains.
- Blocked: work cannot continue until an external decision, dependency, or environment is fixed.
- Open: an active risk remains and its recorded mitigation or external prerequisite is not complete.
- Done: implementation is complete and applicable local/CI acceptance gates pass;
  publication or deployment is tracked separately where required.
- Resolved: a previously open risk or superseded verification item is closed and
  retained only for historical traceability.

explicitly reintroduced later.

## Locked Decisions

- Maintain only three wallet apps: `fearless-iOS`, `fearless-Android`, and `fearless-wallet-web`.
- Keep `fearless-site-web` as the separate public website.
- Wallet core code, registry defaults, and indexer clients must be open source.
- Private overlays may contain only signing keys, store credentials, partner keys,
  analytics keys, and environment-specific release config.
- New wallets use one encrypted universal wallet.
- Default new wallet backup phrase is 24 words.
- Passkey-backed iCloud or Google Drive backup is used where available.
- One phrase restores all supported accounts across Android, iOS, and web.
- Existing users must create or import a universal wallet before using new versions.
- Legacy vaults remain available only for export and fund-safety recovery.
- Users should not need to switch networks manually for normal wallet use.
- Supported ecosystems for this program:
  - Substrate/DOT
  - EVM
  - TON
  - Bitcoin
  - Solana
  - SORA Nexus/Iroha, including Taira testnet
- Bitcoin scope is BIP84 full wallet support.
- Solana scope is wallet support plus browser-extension dApp provider support.
- Solana staking, NFT gallery, and Solana Pay are deferred.
- TON indexer base URL is `https://ti.soramitsu.io`.
- Solana indexer base URL is `https://si.soramitsu.io`.
- SORA2/Polkaswap indexer base URL is `https://pi.soramitsu.io/graphql`.
- The local SORA2/Polkaswap indexer source path is
  `/Users/takemiyamakoto/dev/polkaswap-indexer` (`../polkaswap-indexer` from
  this workspace).
- `si.soramitsu.io` is read-only. Solana simulation and broadcast use configured
  Solana RPC endpoints directly.
- Taira testnet is enabled.
- Nexus mainnet is registry-gated and bound to the documented Minamoto Torii
  source at `https://minamoto.sora.org`; it stays disabled by default until live
  endpoint health and release SDK artifact gates pass.

## Git Flow Standard

### Branches

- `master`: protected releasable branch. No direct pushes. Production releases and
  release tags only.
- `develop`: protected integration branch. Default PR target and default GitHub
  branch for wallet and public-site repos.
- Indexer repos use `master` as the default GitHub branch while retaining
  `develop` for integration work.
- `feature/<ticket>-<slug>`: normal feature work from `develop`.
- `fix/<ticket>-<slug>`: non-production bug fixes from `develop`.
- `chore/<slug>`: tooling, dependency, repo maintenance, and non-feature work.
- `refactor/<slug>`: behavior-preserving refactor work.
- `release/<version>`: short-lived stabilization branch from `develop`.
- `hotfix/<version-or-slug>`: urgent production fix branch from `master`.

### Merge Rules

- Feature, fix, chore, and refactor PRs target `develop`.
- Feature PRs are squash-merged after CI and review.
- Release PRs target `master` and use merge commits to preserve release boundaries.
- Hotfix PRs target `master`, are tagged after merge, then merged or cherry-picked
  back to `develop`.
- Tags must point at commits already on `master`.
- New release tags use SemVer format: `vX.Y.Z`.
- Historical tags stay untouched.

### Branch Protection

- Require PRs for `develop` and `master`.
- Require green CI before merge.
- Require at least one approval.
- Require CODEOWNERS review for wallet core, signing, storage, indexer API, and
  release config once CODEOWNERS is added.
- Disable force-push on protected branches.
- Disable deletion of protected branches.

## Public Wallet Interfaces

### Universal Wallet V2

| Interface | Status | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Shared wallet identity model | Done | Android, iOS, and web now share a versioned public identity envelope with validation and tests. |
| Shared ecosystem enum | Done | Android, iOS, and web now expose the contract IDs: `substrate`, `evm`, `ton`, `bitcoin`, `solana`, `iroha`. |
| Shared chain/indexer registry | Done | Android, iOS, and web now expose a validated shared registry document with Bitcoin, TON, Solana, Taira, and gated Nexus defaults. Platform runtime consumption remains tracked separately. |
| Shared derivation vector fixture format | Done | Added matching Universal Wallet V2 vectors to Android, iOS, and web. |
| Hard-cutoff migration model | Done | Shared Android, iOS, and web migration snapshots now block normal access until a universal wallet exists. |
| Export-only legacy vault mode | Done | Shared legacy vault descriptors enforce export-only access and reject legacy signing. |

### Default Derivations

| Ecosystem | Default derivation | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| EVM | `m/44'/60'/0'/0/0` | Done |
| Bitcoin mainnet | BIP84 `m/84'/0'/0'` | Done |
| Bitcoin testnet | BIP84 `m/84'/1'/0'` | Done |
| Solana | `m/44'/501'/0'/0'` | Done |
| TON | SLIP-0044 coin type `607`, Wallet V4-compatible Ed25519 account | Done |
| SORA Nexus/Iroha | SLIP-0044 coin type `617`, Ed25519/I105 address | Done |
| Taira testnet | I105 discriminant `369` | Done |
| Nexus mainnet | I105 discriminant `753` | Done |

Solana import compatibility should support common existing Solana paths, but the
universal wallet default remains `m/44'/501'/0'/0'`.

all relevant CI checks to be green.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Every maintained repo has `develop` and `master`.
- All normal work enters through short-lived branches and PRs into `develop`.
- `master` is protected, CI-green, tagged for releases, and always releasable.
- One seed phrase restores all supported accounts consistently on Android, iOS,
  and web.
- Bitcoin, TON, Solana, and Taira/Nexus balances and history work from public
  registry config.
- Web extension can connect to Solana dApps and sign supported payloads.
- `ti.soramitsu.io` passes health, service-info, and OpenAPI smoke checks.
- `si.soramitsu.io` serves the Solana/Solswap indexer and passes health,
  service-info, and OpenAPI smoke checks.
- `pi.soramitsu.io/graphql` serves the SORA2/Polkaswap GraphQL indexer, passes
  the PI health identity smoke check, and has ready deployment evidence recorded.
- All three wallet repos and all maintained indexer repos pass CI.
- Every third-party GitHub Action reference is pinned to an immutable commit SHA.
- Passkey backup remains disabled until the challenge service, associated-domain files,
  platform provisioning, and a reviewed cross-device recoverable key source are live.
- Iroha send remains disabled until each platform has a reviewed production Norito codec
  and corresponding live transaction evidence.
- No private secrets or closed-source wallet-core logic are required to build
  public repos.
- Root `scripts/audit-release-readiness.sh` passes without `--skip-live`.

### 2026-07-26 GitHub Governance Fail-Closed Reconciliation

- The root governance audit now validates the complete classic-protection
  contract instead of checking status-context names alone: required checks must
  be strict, administrator enforcement and review-conversation resolution must
  be enabled, force pushes and deletions must remain disabled, and pull-request
  bypass actor lists must be empty. Its apply path preserves existing GitHub App
  check bindings, push restrictions, dismissal restrictions, linear-history and
  branch-lock settings while repairing only missing policy, and it refuses to
  guess when more than one effective repository ruleset applies.
- Active repository-ruleset remediation is implemented for the single-ruleset
  case. It preserves unrelated rules and branch conditions, removes bypass
  actors, and enforces strict required checks, code-owner review, stale-review
  dismissal, last-push approval, one approval, conversation resolution,
  deletion protection, and non-fast-forward protection. Adversarial fixtures
  cover ambiguous rulesets, bypass actors, weak classic policy, malformed
  update payloads, status-check API fallback, and preservation of existing app
  bindings and unrelated protection.
- The stronger read-only audit exposed missing conversation-resolution
  protection on `soramitsu/fearless-site-web` `develop` and `master`. Both
  branches were updated through the official branch-protection API with their
  exact `validate`/`build` GitHub Actions app ID `15368` bindings and all other
  settings preserved. The final fake-API adversarial suite and live read-only
  seven-repository audit pass; evidence is in
  `build/test-results/github-governance-hardening-20260726`.

### 2026-07-26 iOS TestFlight Crash And Migration Hardening

- The installed production-bundle build `4.2.0 (2026.7.23)` was confirmed to terminate
  immediately on the affected phone. Its retained crash report records
  `EXC_BREAKPOINT (SIGTRAP)` on a private `NSManagedObjectContext` queue with
  `_ArrayBuffer._getElementSlowPath -> Array.subscript -> Collection.map ->
  CoreDataRepository.fetchAll`. The source audit found the reachable unchecked
  `cachedPrices[0]` access in `ChainModelMapper` while mapping repository-loaded
  legacy data. That access now uses a safe first-element lookup, and the mapper
  plus the runtime-metadata and chain-cleanup paths have Objective-C exception
  boundaries so malformed legacy Core Data cannot escape as an uncaught startup
  exception.
- User-storage migration now verifies preservation at every model hop before
  destroying the preceding staged store. `StorageMigrator` computes
  bidirectional digests for all common entities, attributes, and relationships;
  its mutation allowlist is empty and fail-closed. Explicit semantic invariants
  cover the intentional v1-to-v2 account-ID deduplication, v9-to-v10 asset
  visibility transformation, and v11-to-v12 filter/favorites transformation.
  New adversarial coverage rejects same-count field mutation, destination
  account deletion, and semantic tampering, including the previously vulnerable
  v2-to-v3 chain-account path.
- Substrate-storage startup now audits child tables directly in raw SQLite
  before Core Data opens them. Every attribute of assets, custom nodes,
  external APIs, chain XCM configuration, price data/providers, and XCM
  assets/destinations is bounded. The fail-closed limits are 256 KiB per child
  value, 256 MiB aggregate child payload, 250,000 rows per child entity, and
  1,000,000 total child rows. Runtime-metadata blobs retain their separate
  larger-payload safety contract. Exact-limit and one-byte/one-row-over
  adversarial cases cover price, asset-name, node, explorer, XCM, provider, and
  aggregate payload paths.

### 2026-07-12 iOS Native TON Builder And Fail-Closed Send Readiness

- Implemented deterministic native TON Wallet V4R2 unsigned fee-emulation and
  signed-transfer construction with separate compile-time message types. Fee
  estimation does not request or derive the mnemonic or private key. Signed
  submission binds the exact BOC, transaction intent, message hash, and raw
  inbound/outbound message bodies; a same-intent retry reuses that exact BOC
  only after an explicit not-found reconciliation result, while ambiguous
  broadcast outcomes preserve the exact message hash.
- Hardened the TonAPI transport boundary with exact-origin bearer authorization,
  strict HTTPS URL validation, redirect rejection, bounded streaming requests
  and responses, propagated cancellation, and exact single-slash request-path
  joining. Cheap pre-parse byte/digit limits now reject oversized sender,
  recipient, amount, and comment inputs before expensive parsing, normalization,
  hashing, or remote work. Private key material is re-derived only after remote
  pre-signing checks instead of being retained across suspension points. The
  earlier builder baseline passed all 100 selected Debug and 56 selected Release
  tests, and the earlier full suites executed 544 Debug tests (498 passed, 46
  intentional skips) and 500 Release tests (454 passed, 46 intentional skips),
  with zero failures. The Release set includes service- and integration-layer
  proofs that submit fails before validation, mnemonic lookup, or remote work.
  Generated-client fixtures prove the
  exact unsigned emulation and broadcast query/path/body contracts, non-2xx
  broadcast rejection, exact-hash reconciliation path, 404-only absence policy,
  malformed and mutated transaction rejection, live null/danger/memo account
  mappings, and trailing-slash base-URL normalization.
- Added durable restart recovery with a versioned, sender-scoped, bounded,
  canonical Keychain journal. Restoration validates sender/public-key ownership,
  the quote digest, strict BOC structure, the Ed25519 signature, and a
  byte-identical fixed-signature rebuild; corrupt, cross-sender, conflicting, or
  unavailable records fail closed. The coordinator journals before exposing a
  signed bearer, checks the stored and current origins for exact equality, and
  performs restored-intent recovery before requesting signing credentials.
  Ordinary quoted submission never automatically rebroadcasts a restored BOC.
  Exact confirmation is first persisted as a terminal tombstone before success
  returns; deletion requires explicit success-UI acknowledgement. Fixed quote-ID
  and canonical-journal SHA-256 vectors plus a structurally valid
  invalid-signature attack bind this persistence contract. Journal updates are
  phase-monotonic, require the exact same bearer, persist before actor-state
  replacement, and deterministically reject a stale recovery that attempts to
  downgrade a confirmed tombstone.
- Added a typed, domain-separated 30-second `TonTransferFeeQuote` that binds the
  reviewed origin, canonical intent, account state, public key, unsigned BOC and
  signing-payload hashes, exact fee, and timing. The transfer layer atomically
  consumes the exact displayed quote; fresh unquoted sends fail before mnemonic
  derivation or remote work, and template, wallet-state, expiry, identity, or
  signed-emulation fee drift fails closed. Signed emulation, broadcast, and
  reconciliation now require the binary-owned exact canonical TonAPI factory,
  with only a DEBUG trusted-test capability. Signed operations also require a
  bounded visible-ASCII reviewed credential. The quote store is synchronous and
  lock-backed, unsubscribe invalidates before cancellation, confirmation is
  enabled only after the exact quote ID is rendered and acknowledged, and the
  MainActor dependency cache keeps estimate and submit on the same TON service.
  Both listener and direct fee estimates stage non-submittable quotes; only the
  exact typed presentation acknowledgement can activate them.
- Added explicit exact-hash unknown-outcome recovery UX in the presenter and all
  nine shipped locales, including strict lowercase 64-hex validation, a
  no-resend warning, and an exact hash copy action. The endpoint/UX focused Debug
  set passed 73/73, the corrected Release arm64 set passed 17/17 with
  `ENABLE_TESTABILITY=YES`, and the new quote/journal/restart focus passed 8/8.
  Swift parse checks, project-file lint, the transaction-builder coverage audit,
  and its exact 120/120 destructive self-test pass. New integration coverage binds
  concurrent dependency-cache reuse, undisplayed-quote rejection, immediate
  unsubscribe revocation, mnemonic-free restart recovery, and malformed
  credential zero-request behavior. A confirmed older intent now surfaces as a
  distinct typed recovery outcome instead of success for a newly requested
  transfer. Friendly sender addresses are canonicalized for exact
  identity/hash acknowledgement, and tombstones remain until the success receipt
  is visibly presented and its callback completes. TON fees render with exact
  asset precision, including the ninth decimal in every tested locale. Fee
  payment resolution pins the selected native TON asset before any unordered
  utility-asset registry fallback, with an extra-utility adversarial regression.
  The final five-fix focused Debug run passed 93/93 and focused Release passed
  25/25, with
  zero failures. The final whole suites executed 568 Debug unit tests (523
  passed and 45 intentionally skipped) and 510 Release unit tests (465 passed
  and 45 intentionally skipped), with zero failures; each configuration also
  intentionally skipped 20 integration tests under the configured gates.
- This local closure does not authorize native TON production send:
  `TonProductionSendReleasePolicy.production` remains immutable and disabled,
  and Release binaries still fail before all send work. Production enablement
  remains Blocked because the pinned TonAPI 0.1.7 contract does not establish
  documented unsigned-ignore-signature versus signed Wallet V4R2 exact fee
  parity or an attested quote; a reviewed local/attested replacement is also not
  present. Independently reviewed endpoint credential provisioning/provenance,
  funded mainnet evidence, and a reviewed finalized-chain absence proof or
  explicit audited quarantine for expired pending intents remain external
  gates. Root plan-readiness now catalogs 4,189 cases, including the 120-case
  iOS contract and the new web, passkey, Bitcoin, and aggregate-boundary
  mutations. The maintained-workspace
  audit is expected to remain red only for owner-controlled external `../iroha`
  source gates after locally stale root expectations are reconciled. A
  head-fenced audit at clean `optimizations` commit
  `fdc40d1165e8afa3b389ae7e3137ad82aa4f5e29` contains 86 unique Iroha-only
  failures and no maintained-workspace failure. Sixty-three rows are newly
  exposed versus the prior 26-row snapshot; three prior exact rows disappeared

  were restored. No positive Iroha source claim is inferred from that checkout.
- Reconfirmed adjacent evidence boundaries without promoting them: the web
  Iroha candidate verifier passes 40 checks, web Iroha readiness passes 36

  scenarios / 91 assertions, and Bitcoin broadcast evidence remains blocked

### 2026-07-12 Wallet Edge-Case, History, And Stub Closure

- Web transaction confirmation now converts only bounded, reviewed error codes
  into localized text. Insufficient balance uses a 20-character safe asset
  symbol or a generic fallback; raw provider/backend text is never rendered.
  Contradictory or malformed responses and rejected promises fail closed and
  cannot leave the popup pending. Google-wallet progress validates safe integer
  bounds, caps allocation at 32 steps, excludes the terminal finish view from
  progress circles, and rejects malformed or out-of-range state without UI
  allocation. `PostMessageProvider` now rejects unsupported manual lifecycle
  calls with a deterministic typed error, validates provider metadata and
  connection notifications, deduplicates concurrent starts, prevents channel
  switching, and fences stale callbacks by generation. Known transaction errors
  use exact `Map` membership, and transaction/provider records require bounded,
  own data fields without invoking inherited accessors or getters. The combined
  additions cover 50 focused positive/negative/adversarial cases; the final web
  unit run passes 372 tests, intentionally skips one, and fails none across 72 files,
  with typecheck, lint, formatting, locale, TODO-debt, and diff checks green.
- Android Giantsquid history now requests only selected GraphQL roots with a
  JSON-escaped, length-bounded account and bounded limit/offset; invalid filters,
  page sizes, and cursors perform no network call. Transfer, reward, slash,
  bond, and bond-and-nominate records use strict bounded amount/timestamp/type
  parsing, deterministic newest-first ordering, global ID deduplication, and an
  overflow-safe continuation cursor only when a selected root fills the page.
  The 11 focused tests pass in both Debug and Release and cover injection,
  impossible dates, long fractions, oversized amounts/types, nullable success,
  duplicate/reordered records, filter isolation, pagination, and invalid bounds.
  The complete feature-wallet unit suite also passes 91/91 in each variant.
- Android pool rewards no longer rewrite either retired demo chain ID to
  Polkadot: start and active pool screens pass the exact selected `ChainId`,
  amount, period, and compound flag once, while failures and cancellation
  propagate without fallback retry. Staking network information and bodies now
  map Pool, RelayChain, and Parachain models against the current selection and
  reject stale cross-scenario replay. Relay nominator/validator/stash-none and
  Parachain welcome/delegator bodies replace the former empty Compose stubs with
  localized stake, reward, status, action, and setup routing. Missing candidate
  or round data preserves a visible recovery card, ready-to-unlock takes status
  precedence, and timer calculations use bounded `BigInteger` arithmetic with a
  nonnegative ten-year display ceiling. Countdown content now reaches the timer
  before auxiliary text, and completion is delivered exactly once. Solana RPC
  error codes now use explicit signed-`Int` bounds on every supported Android
  API, and Bitcoin/Solana/Iroha connected-account labels are present in all
  seven translated resource sets. Twenty-nine focused staking/common positive,
  negative, and adversarial tests pass. Full
  Debug and Release feature-staking suites pass 45/45 each and common passes
  184/184 in each variant; feature-staking and common lint pass both variants
  with no error.
- iOS validator analytics replaces its literal placeholder with the existing
  localized received-rewards label in all nine locales. Reward allocation is
  exact-stash, reward-only, nominated-validator-only, unique-event, BigUInt-first,
  finite, clamped, and zero-safe; malformed account IDs, unsupported precision,
  extreme conversion, reversed ranges, and out-of-range eras fail closed. Live
  Arrowsquid and Subquery reward adapters now validate query inputs before
  networking, use their actual history schemas, bind exact outer and nested
  stash/delegator identities, and carry validator plus era attribution end to
  end. Canonical unsigned reward amounts are capped at 78 decimal digits before
  `BigUInt`; malformed attribution retains aggregate rewards only through the
  explicit blank/zero sentinel that per-validator analytics rejects. Seventeen
  focused tests pass in both Debug and arm64 Release. The full Debug suite passes

  localization validation, TODO checks, and diff checks are green. Polkadot and

- Root plan-readiness now catalogs 4,189 cases. The prior 60 additions plus the

  and forged/clean controls, wallet error/progress/provider boundaries,

### 2026-07-10 Android XCM Effective Runtime Trust And Evidence Closure

- Closed the mutable-registry trust gap. Android release execution now derives
  authority from an immutable APK-owned 15-route per-asset registry and uses
  remote chain discovery only to remove routes from that authority. Remote
  execution metadata, persisted Room state, caller-supplied chain lookalikes,
  extra fee assets, nonzero fee indexes, noncanonical XCM versions, estimated
  destination fees, bridge modes, and unapproved assets all fail closed.
- The production discovery input is a successful current-process sync snapshot.
  It is cleared before every refresh, remains unavailable while refresh is in
  flight or after failure, and is published only after canonical fetch and
  database application both succeed. Production DI cannot fall back to a stale
  process or persisted snapshot.
- Release builds use the literal canonical shared-features URL and expose no
  release URL override. `ENABLE_PRODUCTION_XCM_TRANSFERS` is literal `false` in
  release builds; only debug builds accept the strict debug-only flag. Disabled
  release DI exposes neither the XCM engine nor discovery and does not read the
  approved-route asset.
- Hardened the effective-registry report and production-evidence contracts. A
  ready claim must first regenerate a canonical live discovery report, prove
  complete approved/required/effective route parity with exact byte-length and
  SHA-256 bindings for the APK registry, required-route manifest, and bundled
  chain registry, and preserve the fail-closed policy. Evidence then requires
  finalized origin and destination block proofs, successful origin extrinsic
  and destination event results, a positive destination balance delta, distinct
  public HTTPS proof URLs, canonical RPC/explorer verification, a non-future
  verification timestamp, an independent verifier distinct from the operator,
  and Android release-commit binding. The audit validates the attestation
  contract; release reviewers must still verify the linked proofs independently.

  112 production-evidence scenarios (110 negative and 2 valid-state); registry
  adversarial and real-manifest audits; 70 public XCM, 10 runtime discovery, and
  3 wallet-DI unit tests; and the release Kotlin compile across 507 Gradle tasks.

  discovered route candidates, 13 compatible approved candidates, 2 approved

### 2026-06-23 Native Bitcoin Fee Selection Foundation

- Added Android `BitcoinFeeEstimator` over `BitcoinIndexerClient.feeEstimates`.
- Added iOS `BitcoinFeeEstimator` over `BitcoinIndexerClientProtocol` and wired
  it into the Xcode app and test targets.
- Matched the existing web Bitcoin send-service fee policy:
  - default target is 2 blocks;
  - target must be between 1 and 1008 blocks;
  - estimates with non-positive, non-finite, or non-integer block targets are
    ignored;
  - exact targets are preferred, otherwise the next slower target is selected,
    with slowest available as fallback;
  - fee rates must be finite, positive, and no more than 10,000 sat/vB.

### 2026-06-23 Native Bitcoin UTXO Selection Foundation

- Added Android `BitcoinUtxoSelector` to validate Esplora UTXOs, filter
  confirmed spendable UTXOs by default, estimate P2WPKH transaction vsize, and
  select deterministic inputs for a spend plan.
- Added iOS `BitcoinUtxoSelector` with matching behavior and wired it into the
  Xcode app and test targets.
- Matched the existing web Bitcoin send-service policy:
  - P2WPKH dust threshold is 330 sats;
  - estimated vsize is `11 + inputs * 68 + outputs * 31`;
  - UTXOs sort by value descending, then txid, then vout;
  - exact no-change spends are allowed;
  - uneconomical dust change is absorbed into the fee;
  - change is emitted only when it is at or above dust.

  - deterministic highest-value selection and fee/change calculation;

  - insufficient funds and max-input rejection;

### 2026-06-23 Native Solana SOL Send Service Foundation

- Added Android and iOS native legacy System Program SOL transfer transaction
  builders.
- Builders now produce deterministic unsigned transfer envelopes with:
  - one required signer;
  - sender, recipient, and System Program account keys;
  - caller-provided recent blockhash;
  - compiled System Program `transfer` instruction data;
  - base64 transaction and message payloads for signer/RPC handoff.

  - validate lamports and recipient addresses before RPC calls;
  - derive the Universal Wallet V2 Solana sender;
  - fetch a latest blockhash through configured Solana RPC;
  - request `getFeeForMessage` for the unsigned message;
  - sign the transfer with the existing serialized transaction signer;
  - simulate the signed transfer before broadcast by default;
  - broadcast through `sendTransaction`;

    first signature.

### 2026-06-24 Native Solana Deterministic ATA Derivation

- Added deterministic Associated Token Account derivation to Android and iOS
  Solana transaction builders using the official Solana PDA seed layout:
  wallet public key, token program id, mint public key, and the Associated
  Token Program id.
- Android uses Bouncy Castle Ed25519 public-key validation to reject on-curve
  PDA candidates while searching bump seeds from `255` down to `0`.
- iOS uses the existing `BigInt` dependency plus SHA-256 to perform Ed25519
  decompression/square-root validation locally; CryptoKit alone was not used
  for this check because it accepts off-curve PDA bytes as public keys.
- `buildCreateAssociatedTokenAccount` now derives the ATA when no ATA is
  supplied and rejects caller-supplied ATAs that do not match the deterministic
  wallet/mint/token-program address.
- `buildTokenSendChecked` and `SolanaTokenSendRequest` now allow token sends to
  omit `destinationTokenAccount` when `destinationWalletAddress` is supplied;
  the builders derive the correct SPL Token or Token-2022 ATA.
- Added Android and iOS tests for:
  - canonical SPL Token destination-wallet ATA:
    `BNrmzq2GNxwxHf8dSiaEJdtUiQBg4VGCFi9ovhAK6WrK`;
  - canonical Token-2022 destination-wallet ATA:
    `2bFPe5wRzpinUSyFT42imC5DFHtEFugZ6UhgBeWRRxhH`;
  - automatic ATA use in create/send builders;
  - mismatched supplied ATA rejection;
  - existing duplicate-account and malformed-address adversarial cases.
- Verification completed:
  - `fearless-iOS`: targeted `swiftc -typecheck` for
    `SolanaTransferTransactionBuilder.swift` with a temporary BigInt module.
  - `fearless-iOS`: targeted `swiftc -parse` for touched Solana source and
    tests.
  - `fearless-iOS`: compiled and ran a small executable against the Swift
    builder; derived SPL and Token-2022 ATA outputs matched the canonical
    vectors above.
  - Android and iOS: scoped `git diff --check`, conflict-marker scans, and
    trailing-whitespace scans for the touched Solana builder/send/test files.
- Local verification blockers remain:
  - `fearless-Android`: Gradle/JVM tests cannot run because this machine has no
    Java runtime installed.
  - `fearless-iOS`: full XCTest/package verification is still blocked by the
    existing `https://github.com/DRadmir/ton-swift.git` SwiftPM

### 2026-06-24 Native Solana ATA Existence Checks

- Added native Solana `getAccountInfo` wrappers to Android and iOS RPC clients:
  - `accountExists(address, commitment, rpcUrl)` on Android.
  - `accountExists(address:commitment:rpcURL:)` on iOS.
- The wrappers validate public-key-shaped account addresses before network
  calls and treat `value: null` as missing, `value: { ... }` as present, and
  malformed account-info envelopes as typed RPC errors.
- Updated native SPL Token and Token-2022 send services to derive the
  destination wallet ATA before transaction assembly:
  - if the ATA exists on chain, the services send directly to it with one
    `TransferChecked` instruction and do not include rent in the SOL balance
    sufficiency check;
  - if the ATA is missing, the services keep the idempotent ATA-create
    instruction before `TransferChecked` and include the rent-exemption quote
    when a balance provider is configured;
  - if a caller supplies both a destination wallet and a mismatched destination
    token account, the services reject the request before the account-existence
    RPC lookup.
- Added Android and iOS coverage for:
  - RPC request construction and response normalization for existing and
    missing accounts;
  - malformed account-info responses and invalid account addresses;
  - missing ATA token sends that include the create instruction;
  - existing ATA token sends that skip the create instruction;
  - rent inclusion only when an ATA-create instruction is actually present;
  - mismatched supplied ATA rejection.
- Verification completed:
  - `fearless-iOS`: `xcrun swiftc -parse -parse-as-library` for touched Solana
    RPC/send source and tests.
  - `fearless-iOS`: `xcrun swiftc -typecheck -parse-as-library` for Solana RPC
    source plus local transport/registry dependencies.
  - `fearless-iOS`: broader `xcrun swiftc -typecheck -parse-as-library` over
    Solana indexer, balance, transfer builder, signer, transaction signer, RPC,
    and send service source files with the existing temporary BigInt module.
  - Android and iOS: scoped `git diff --check` and conflict-marker scans for
    the touched Solana RPC/send files and tests.
- Local verification blockers remain:
  - `fearless-Android`: Gradle/JVM tests cannot run because this machine has no
    Java runtime installed.
  - `fearless-iOS`: full XCTest/package verification is still blocked by the

  address under the transfer-hook program id.

  - non-transferable Token-2022 mints are rejected before RPC calls;
  - transfer-fee Token-2022 mints require an explicit fee acknowledgement before
    a send is prepared;

    a send is prepared.

    `TransferChecked`, with the configured fee withheld on the destination
    account.
  - Solana Transfer Hook docs state that token transfers must include all extra
    accounts required by the hook instruction.

### 2026-06-24 TON Indexer Outage Fallback

- Added TON balance outage fallback in the web extension:
  - native TON balance refreshes reuse the last cached balance when the TON
    indexer/API path is unavailable;
  - cached native balances are marked `ERROR` during the failed refresh instead
    of being overwritten as ready zero balances;
  - cached jetton balances are preserved and marked `ERROR` during failed
    jetton refreshes.
- Added TON history outage fallback in the web extension:
  - the last successful TON history response is cached in memory per
    network/address;
  - failed history refreshes return a cloned cached response, preventing caller
    mutation from corrupting the fallback cache;
  - accounts without cached history still receive an empty TON history envelope.
- Added negative unit coverage for unavailable TI/API responses, missing balance
  cache, cached native/jetton fallback, and history cache mutation isolation.

### 2026-06-24 Web Solana Native SOL Transfer

- Added a browser-safe Solana SystemProgram SOL transfer adapter for the web
  extension:
  - builds canonical legacy transfer transactions without adding `@solana/web3.js`;
  - converts SOL amounts to lamports with `bigint` and rejects whitespace,
    exponent notation, zero values, excessive precision, and values outside the
    unsigned 64-bit lamport range;
  - validates 32-byte base58 source, recipient, and blockhash values;
  - resolves Universal Wallet Solana source metadata from stored wallet
    accounts and verifies the exported mnemonic derives the expected Solana
    public key before signing;
  - estimates fees through the selected Solana RPC endpoint from runtime
    network providers/nodes;
  - simulates the signed transaction with signature verification before
    broadcast;
  - rejects broadcasts whose returned signature does not match the locally
    signed transaction signature;
  - schedules a Solana balance refresh after successful broadcast.
- Wired web background `checkTransfer` and `makeTransfer` so Solana networks no
  longer fall through to Substrate/EVM/TON transfer handling.
- Kept this path intentionally limited to native `SOL`. SPL Token and
  Token-2022 sends remain tracked under the broader Solana send-flow work.
- Added adversarial tests for malformed amounts, malformed addresses, source
  mnemonic mismatch, unsupported assets, unavailable fee responses, simulation
  failure, signature mismatch, and post-send balance refresh behavior.

### 2026-06-24 Web Standard SPL Token Send Construction

- Extended the web Solana transfer adapter from native-SOL-only to support
  standard SPL Token sends when stored SI balance metadata is complete and
  unambiguous.
- The web token send path now:
  - resolves source token account, mint, decimals, account state, and token
    program from the persisted Solana balance item;
  - supports only the legacy SPL Token program
    `TokenkegQfeZyiNwAJbNbGKPFXCWuBvf9Ss623VQ5DA`;
  - derives the recipient associated token account from recipient wallet owner,
    token program, and mint using the official Solana PDA seed layout;
  - prepends idempotent associated-token-account creation before
    `TransferChecked`;
  - normalizes token amounts as base units without floating point arithmetic;
  - estimates fees, signs, simulates, broadcasts, and schedules balance refresh
    through the existing Solana RPC send pipeline.
- Kept Token-2022, transfer-fee, transfer-hook, frozen, extension-bearing, and
  incomplete-token-metadata sends fail-closed before any RPC blockhash or fee
  call.
- Added a direct `@noble/curves` dependency because Ed25519 curve checks are
  required for browser-side PDA derivation and the package was previously only
  present transitively.
- Added focused coverage for:
  - deterministic ATA derivation vectors for the source and recipient wallets;
  - token amount parsing and `u64` bounds;
  - raw SPL Token transaction account ordering, compiled instruction indexes,
    idempotent ATA instruction data, and `TransferChecked` instruction data;
  - fee-estimation metadata lookup through `balanceService.getTokenBalance`;
  - signed/simulated/broadcast token sends and post-send balance refresh;
  - unsupported Token-2022/extensions/fee-hook/malformed metadata rejecting
    before RPC.

### 2026-06-24 Web Bitcoin History Pagination

- The fetcher now:
  - walks `/address/{wallet}/txs` and `/address/{wallet}/txs/chain/{txid}`;

    pages with no new transactions.

  plain Bitcoin `HistoryElement[]`.

  - hostile repeated pages with duplicate cursors;
  - hard pagination cap when every page is full.

### 2026-06-24 Android Hard-Cutoff Migration Snapshot Builder

- Added a pure Android migration snapshot builder over `LightMetaAccount`
  projections so app code can compute the shared hard-cutoff state from public
  account metadata without reading mnemonic, seed, or private-key material.
- The builder now emits shared `UniversalWalletMigrationSnapshot` payloads with:
  - `create-universal-wallet` for empty installs;
  - `migrate-before-access` plus export-only legacy vault descriptors for
    pre-cutoff Substrate, EVM, and TON root account material;

    present: Substrate, EVM, TON, Bitcoin, Solana, and Iroha.

  sanitized display names, `canExportSecrets = true`, and
  `canSignTransactions = false`.
- Malformed public account data now stays fail-closed by producing a valid
  non-secret `unavailable:*` display address instead of unlocking normal access
  or emitting an invalid migration snapshot.
- Added Android JVM coverage for:
  - empty installs;
  - legacy root-account export-only descriptors;
  - complete Universal Wallet normal access;
  - partial Universal Wallet material staying blocked;
  - partial Universal Wallet material preserving legacy export descriptors;
  - malformed legacy data producing a valid fail-closed descriptor.

  targets without enabling legacy signing.

    account ID format for a local light account;

  to current Android legacy root-secret export routes.

  - resolving Substrate, EVM, and TON descriptors to existing export chain IDs;
  - rejecting descriptors with signing enabled or export disabled;
  - rejecting tampered deterministic IDs;
  - rejecting unsupported Universal Wallet ecosystems;
  - rejecting descriptors whose matching local account lacks root material.

### 2026-06-24 iOS Legacy Vault Export Resolver

- Added a pure iOS legacy-vault export resolver that maps shared
  `UniversalWalletLegacyVaultDescriptor` entries to existing native export
  targets without enabling legacy signing.
- The resolver only returns a target when:
  - the descriptor is valid `export-only` metadata with
    `canExportSecrets = true` and `canSignTransactions = false`;
  - the descriptor vault/account IDs and display address match the
    deterministic iOS legacy account format for a local wallet;
  - the local wallet still has root material for the requested ecosystem;
  - the ecosystem is supported by the existing iOS root export stack:
    Substrate or EVM.
- TON, Bitcoin, Solana, and Iroha descriptors stay unresolved on iOS because
  they do not map to current iOS legacy root-secret export routes.
- Added XCTest coverage for:
  - resolving Substrate and EVM descriptors to existing export chain IDs;
  - rejecting descriptors with signing enabled or export disabled;
  - rejecting tampered deterministic IDs or display addresses;
  - rejecting unsupported Universal Wallet ecosystems;
  - rejecting descriptors whose matching local wallet lacks root material.

  recovery UX, revocation/deletion behavior, and platform entitlements.

### 2026-06-25 Android Passkey Google Drive Storage Adapter

- Added an Android Google Drive `appDataFolder` storage adapter for encrypted
  passkey backup in `public-shared-features-backup`:
  - `GoogleDriveAccessTokenProvider` keeps Google account/token acquisition
    injectable and outside unit tests.
  - `GoogleDriveHttpTransport` and `OkHttpGoogleDriveHttpTransport` isolate
    live HTTP execution from Drive protocol behavior.
  - `GoogleDrivePasskeyBackupDriveClient` lists, creates, updates, downloads,
    and deletes Drive files using the Drive v3 appdata scope
    `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/drive.appdata`.
  - `GoogleDrivePasskeyBackupCloudStorage` implements the existing
    `PasskeyBackupCloudStorage` contract and stores only already-encrypted
    payload bytes.

    versions, invalid storage keys, empty downloads, unauthorized responses, and
    malformed file-list responses.
- Added `gson`, `okhttp`, and coroutine test dependencies to the backup module
  for the Drive adapter and deterministic unit tests.
- Expanded the root passkey prerequisite audit so Android now explicitly
  requires the Drive appdata scope and a Google Drive appDataFolder adapter, not
  just a placeholder cloud-storage interface.

### 2026-06-25 Android Passkey Backup Workflow

- Added `PasskeyBackupWorkflow` in the Android public backup module as the
  app-facing orchestration seam for passkey-backed cloud backup:
  - `beginRegistration` obtains a remote WebAuthn registration challenge and
    returns pending registration state plus request JSON;
  - `finishRegistration` completes the remote ceremony, verifies the returned
    storage key matches the pending registration, then saves the already
    encrypted payload to cloud storage;
  - `beginRestore` obtains a remote assertion challenge for a normalized storage
    key and returns pending assertion state plus request JSON;
  - `finishRestore` completes the assertion ceremony, verifies the returned
    storage key, then loads the encrypted cloud backup;
  - `deleteBackup` normalizes the storage key before deleting cloud backup data.
- Changed pending Android passkey ceremony DTOs to carry raw request JSON as the
  primary testable contract and expose thin `createRequest()` / `createOption()`
  helpers for the Credential Manager UI layer. This avoids Android `Bundle`
  calls in JVM unit tests while keeping the production integration point.
- Added `PasskeyBackupWorkflowTest` with adversarial coverage for:
  - registration request construction from a remote challenge;
  - registration completion saving encrypted payload only after a matching
    storage key;
  - restore request construction from a remote assertion challenge;
  - restore completion loading cloud payload only after a matching storage key;
  - mismatched storage keys and missing cloud payloads failing closed;
  - normalized deletion and unsupported RP rejection.
- Strengthened the passkey prerequisite audit so Android now must expose the
  workflow seam, and expanded its adversarial self-test with a fixture that
  removes the workflow and fails.

### 2026-06-25 Mobile Passkey Backup Identity Envelope Guard

- Hardened the mobile passkey backup cloud record contract so encrypted backup
  blobs are bound to explicit recovery metadata:
  - storage key;
  - wallet id;
  - normalized account name;
  - positive `createdAtMillis`;
  - schema version.
- Android changes:
  - `PasskeyBackupEncryptedPayload` now requires `walletId`, `accountName`,
    and `createdAtMillis` metadata in addition to storage key and encrypted
    bytes;
  - `PasskeyBackupWorkflow` validates and carries the selected wallet/account
    through pending registration and stamps the saved payload with an injectable
    creation clock;
  - `GoogleDrivePasskeyBackupDriveClient` writes those fields to Drive
    `appProperties`, reloads them before trusting downloaded bytes, and rejects
    missing metadata, storage-key mismatches, malformed accounts, invalid
    timestamps, duplicate files, unsupported schema versions, and empty payloads.
- iOS changes:
  - `PasskeyBackupEncryptedRecord` now requires the same identity envelope;
  - `PasskeyBackupWorkflow` preserves selected wallet/account metadata through
    registration and stamps saved CloudKit records with an injectable creation
    clock;
  - `CloudKitPasskeyBackupCloudStorage` writes and validates `storageKey`,
    `walletId`, `accountName`, and `createdAtMillis` fields before returning a
    restored encrypted record.

  `encryptedBackupMetadata` envelope and strengthened
  `scripts/audit-passkey-backup-prerequisites.sh` plus its adversarial fixture
  test so removing platform metadata fields, Drive metadata validation, or

  - amounts at or below zero are rejected;

  - empty sender account ids and blank recipients are rejected.

  fail-closed behavior, unavailable fee/transfer paths, unsupported route
  assets, below-minimum amounts, blank recipients, empty senders, and same-chain
  transfers.

  - `XcmExecutionSpec` now captures the backend-critical route fields that were
    previously missing from discovery metadata: pallet/call identity, transfer
    mode, route XCM version, asset/beneficiary/fee multilocations, fee-asset
    index, weight-limit policy, destination-fee policy, and optional bridge
    execution metadata.
  - Android chain JSON/runtime models can now carry optional
    `Chain.Xcm.Destination.execution` metadata without breaking existing route
    catalogs; missing execution metadata remains fail-closed.
  - `XcmExecutionSpecValidator` rejects blank call fields, unsupported transfer
    modes, malformed multilocations, negative fee indexes, invalid limited or
    unlimited weight-limit combinations, invalid destination-fee policies, and
    bridge execution specs that do not match route `bridgeParachainId`.
- Hardened the public XCM service boundary:
  - `XcmTransferRequest` includes the validated `executionSpec`, so future
    backends cannot submit with raw discovery-only metadata.
  - `getXcmOriginFee` validates and forwards the route execution spec before
    delegating to the backend.
  - `isXcmSupportAsset` now requires both an available backend and at least one
    executable route for the asset; missing or malformed execution specs keep
    transfer support hidden.
- Added adversarial unit coverage:
  - service rejects missing execution specs before engine calls;
  - service rejects malformed execution specs before engine calls;
  - service does not advertise support for missing or malformed execution specs;
  - route fetcher returns validated executable routes;
  - route fetcher fails closed for missing specs, malformed limited
    weight-limit specs, and mismatched bridge execution metadata.
- Strengthened `scripts/audit-plan-readiness.sh` and
  `scripts/test-plan-readiness-audit.sh` so Android readiness now fails if the
  execution-spec model, validator, executable-route lookup, support-advertising
  guard, or new adversarial XCM tests are removed.

### 2026-06-26 Iroha JS Native Transaction Payload Hardening

- Hardened `../iroha` JS SDK transaction submission so
  `ToriiClient.submitTransaction` uses the native signed-transaction Norito
  encoder when available, preserves native versioned transaction payloads, and
  still falls back to the prior version-byte wrapper for opaque or foreign signed
  payload bytes. Native transaction encoding is opportunistic, so submit fallback
  remains usable when the local native binding is absent or fails checksum
  verification.
- Added a per-client native binding test hook so submit-path tests no longer
  share `globalThis.__IROHA_NATIVE_BINDING__` state across the broad Node suite.
- Expanded adversarial submit-transaction coverage for native Norito wrapping,
  native versioned payload preservation, native encoder rejection fallback,
  NRT0 deframing, retry behavior, pipeline 405 rejection, and the removed public
  submit route.
- Fixed the native privacy FFI parity guard to accept stable `#[unsafe(no_mangle)]`

### 2026-06-26 Iroha SCCP Route Manifest Raw Pipeline Publishing

  publication submits the already signed transaction to Torii
  `/v1/pipeline/transactions` as an `application/x-norito` payload with the
  expected version byte prefix, instead of relying on the generic JS transaction
  submit helper.
- The publication command now:
  - records raw pipeline HTTP acceptance metadata in public submission evidence;
  - polls `GET /v1/pipeline/transactions/status` when `--wait-for-commit` is
    enabled;
  - treats `Applied`, `Committed`, `Rejected`, `Failed`, and `Expired` as
    terminal status kinds, while still requiring `Applied` before publication is
    successful;
  - surfaces a bounded response-body preview for non-2xx raw pipeline
    submission failures without logging private key material.
- Added adversarial route-manifest publication tests proving:
  - the raw pipeline payload has the `application/x-norito` contract and
    versioned signed-transaction bytes;
  - default `--wait-for-commit` records an `Applied` status and polls by the
    submitted transaction hash;
  - terminal non-`Applied` statuses fail and still write non-secret submission
    evidence;
  - raw pipeline HTTP failures include a diagnostic preview without secret
    leakage.

### 2026-06-26 Passkey Evidence Ordering And Secret-Leak Hardening

- Hardened the passkey deployment-evidence audit so public release evidence also:
  - rejects `smokePassedAt` values earlier than `deployedAt`, preventing
    impossible live-smoke evidence from satisfying `--require-ready`;
  - recursively rejects secret-like or credential-store snapshot fields such as
    `privateKey`, `token`, `authorization`, `clientDataJSON`, and
    `credentialsByStorageKey` anywhere in the public evidence JSON;
  - rejects unsupported non-secret fields at the top level, within
    `deploymentEvidence[]`, within `healthResponse`, and within
    `platformProvisioning`, so public release evidence cannot drift by silently
    accumulating unreviewed schema fields;
  - rejects duplicate `deploymentEvidence[].deploymentId` values so a copied
    deployment record cannot be counted as independent production evidence;
  - requires the full release command contract in the committed manifest,
    including syntax checks, service tests, Docker build, deployment evidence
    template generation, static/ready deployment audits, and live health smoke.
- Expanded adversarial coverage in
  `services/passkey-backup-challenge-service/scripts/test-deployment-evidence-audit.sh`
  for smoke-before-deploy timestamps, top-level secret-like evidence keys, and
  nested health-response credential leaks.
- Added unsupported-field adversarial fixtures for:
  - top-level evidence fields;
  - per-deployment evidence fields;
  - health response fields;
  - platform provisioning fields;
  - duplicate deployment IDs;
  - missing required release commands such as `npm test` and the Docker build.
- Updated the passkey service audit and root plan-readiness audit/self-test so
  the timestamp-order, unsupported-field, duplicate-ID, complete-command, and
  secret-leak gates cannot be removed silently.

### 2026-06-25 Android XCM Route-Aware Destination Fees

- Hardened the public Android XCM destination-fee path so it now requires the
  origin chain id, destination chain id, asset, and validated route execution
  spec before returning any fee.
- Updated `XcmService.getXcmDestinationFee` to resolve the executable route
  first, reject blank/same-chain requests, and avoid incorrectly applying
  transfer `minAmount` checks to fee-only lookups.
- Implemented deterministic destination-fee semantics in
  `SubstrateXcmTransferEngine`:
  - `INCLUDED` returns zero;
  - `FIXED` normalizes the integer route amount by `Asset.precision`;
  - `ESTIMATED` remains fail-closed until a real destination estimator is
    implemented;
  - mismatched destination-fee asset symbols are rejected before any value is
    returned.

  cross-chain quick inputs, and the setup screen destination-fee flow.
- Strengthened root plan-readiness so the aggregate release gate now requires
  included-fee, fixed-fee, estimated-fail-closed, and asset-mismatch destination
  fee tests, plus an adversarial self-test that fails if fixed-fee coverage is
  removed.

### 2026-06-25 Android Public XCM Backend Wiring

- Added a concrete open-source Android XCM backend in
  `public-shared-features-xcm`:
  - `SubstrateXcmTransferEngine` implements `XcmTransferEngine`;
  - `XcmExtrinsicSubmitter` is a testable submission seam;
  - `ExtrinsicServiceXcmSubmitter` wraps the existing public
    `ExtrinsicService` with the per-origin `KeypairProvider` supplied by
    `XcmInteractor.prepareDataForChains`.
- Added `destinationLocation` to the Android XCM execution metadata model,
  remote JSON model, mapper, runtime validator, registry audit, and adversarial
  audit fixture. This closes the previous ambiguity where executable metadata
  had asset, beneficiary, and fee multilocations but not the destination
  multilocation required to build a production XCM call.
- The backend now builds versioned XCM extrinsic calls from validated metadata:
  - maps `destinationLocation`, `beneficiaryLocation`, and `assetLocation` into
    versioned multilocation call arguments;
  - builds fungible asset transfer arguments with the selected amount;
  - includes `weight_limit` only for limited transfer types;
  - replaces `<account>` placeholders with the runtime recipient address;
  - rejects blank recipients, invalid `v<number>` XCM versions, missing keypair
    providers, invalid keypair-provider objects, and origin-chain mismatches
    before reaching the submitter.
- Wired `WalletFeatureModule.provideXcmService` to construct `XcmService` with
  `SubstrateXcmTransferEngine(ExtrinsicServiceXcmSubmitter(...))` instead of the
  unavailable default engine. The unavailable default remains available for
  tests and fail-closed construction.
- Expanded adversarial backend coverage in `SubstrateXcmTransferEngineTest`:
  - limited reserve transfer call planning and submission;
  - non-limited transfer calls omitting weight limits;
  - origin-fee estimation through the submitter;
  - missing/invalid keypair provider rejection before submission;
  - invalid XCM version and blank recipient rejection before submission;
  - destination-fee estimation remains fail-closed without route context;
  - origin-chain mismatch rejection before fee estimation.
- Strengthened root plan-readiness so release gates now fail if the concrete
  backend, backend tests, destination-location contract, destination-location
  registry negative test, or Android DI wiring are removed.

  origin fee asset precision instead of the transferred asset precision.

  explicit `originFeeAsset`.

  asset into origin-fee estimation, and updated cross-chain confirmation
  validation to convert `transferDraft.originFee` through the utility asset
  token configuration before checking available balances.

    USDT returns `0.000000012345`, not `12345`;
  - negative origin-fee asset precision is rejected before submitter calls;
  - origin-fee assets from another chain are rejected before submitter calls;
  - `XcmService` records and forwards the separate origin-fee asset.

    validation;

### 2026-06-29 Release Blocker Classification In Action Manifests

- Extended release blocker actions, `blockers.md`, `manifest.json`, and
  `unblock.md` with two required fields for every failed check:
  `unblockCategory` and `externalPrerequisite`.
- `unblockCategory` now separates local code work from external release
  prerequisites. Current supported categories include `review-and-merge`,
  `deployment-evidence`, `live-service-deployment`,
  `live-service-and-evidence`, `live-service-routing`,
  `funded-route-evidence`, `funded-broadcast-evidence`,
  `private-overlay-cleanup`, `upstream-dependency`, `github-admin`, and
  `local-code`.

  - `release-pr-readiness` is `review-and-merge`, requiring reviewer
    approvals, resolved GitHub review conversations, and protected-branch
    merges.
  - `passkey-deployment-evidence`, `ti-deployment-evidence`, and
    `si-deployment-evidence` are `deployment-evidence`, requiring production
    deployment or registry evidence before release.
  - `passkey-backup-prerequisites` and `ti-production-smoke` are
    `live-service-deployment`, requiring live DNS/routing/deployment fixes.
  - `iroha-release-readiness` is `live-service-and-evidence`, requiring
    healthy Minamoto Nexus Torii plus route publication, canary, and wallet
    transfer evidence.
  - `android-xcm-production-evidence` is `funded-route-evidence`, and
    `web-bitcoin-broadcast-evidence` is `funded-broadcast-evidence`.
  - `si-production-smoke` is `live-service-routing`, requiring
    `si.soramitsu.io` to route to the Solana/Solswap indexer instead of the
    TON indexer.

  - `scripts/audit-plan-readiness.sh` now requires the classifiers, report
